Monday
My stomach hurt again this morning, right when I was tying my shoes. It always hurts on school days, never on Sundays. Mummy gave me ajwain water and said I eat too fast.
In class Tejas called me Sumit Snotty again and everyone laughed. Maybe it's because I'm slow at kabaddi. Maybe if I was funnier they would stop. I think it's my fault somehow.
Urmila didi asked why her little brother looks so sad these days. I said "nothing, tests." If I tell Mummy, she will go to school and shout, and then Tejas will know I told, and it will be worse.
So I just won't say anything.
Sumit

passage: Every morning at the bus stop outside Sirsa, Pawan held his stomach. "Again?" his mother Vandana asked, tying his tiffin. "Just a little," he said. He thought about the time Papa went to the sarpanch over a small fight and the whole village talked for weeks. No. If he told, everything would get bigger. He pulled the blanket up and stayed quiet.

passage:
Every school morning in their Kolkata flat, Abhinav's stomach hurt at exactly 7:15, when he tied his shoes.

"Again?" his mother Vandana asked, touching his forehead. No fever.

He couldn't tell her about the boys who called him "Dhobi" and threw his cap on the fan. If he told, she'd go to school, and then they'd know he told, and it would get worse. And maybe it was his fault anyway. Maybe his cap was stupid.

So he said, "Just a stomach ache, Ma," and went.

On Friday, Vandana found the cap in his bag, torn along the brim. She didn't shout. That night she sat on his bed and said, "Something is happening at school. You can tell me, and I won't do anything without asking you first."

Abhinav's eyes filled. He started talking.

qa.q: At what time did Abhinav's stomach hurt every school morning?
qa.a: At exactly 7:15, when he tied his shoes.

qa.q: Why did Abhinav hide the bullying from his mother?
qa.a: He felt afraid it would get worse if he told, and ashamed, thinking it might be his own fault.

qa.q: What did Vandana do that helped Abhinav open up?
qa.a: She noticed the torn cap, stayed calm, and promised not to act without asking him first, so telling felt safe.

qa.q: How might Vandana have felt finding the torn cap?
qa.a: She was probably worried and upset, but chose to stay calm so Abhinav wouldn't feel more afraid.

grounding: Abhinav has stomach aches before school and hides the bullying out of fear and shame, until his mother gently makes it safe to tell.

"Vikas, why aren't you eating?"

"Not hungry, Noor didi."

"You said that yesterday. And you had a stomach ache on Monday."

"It's just my stomach."

"Only on school days?"

"...Yes."

"Vikas. Is someone bothering you?"

"No."

"You can tell me."

"If I tell, you'll tell Ammi, and Ammi will go to school, and then Sameer will know I told."

"So it's Sameer."

"...He takes my tiffin. Every day. He says I'm a baby who needs his mummy's food."

"That's not your fault."

"Maybe it is. Maybe I am a baby."

"You're not. Listen. We'll tell Ammi together, tonight, and we'll ask her to talk to your teacher quietly. You won't be alone."

qa.a: His tiffin.

When I was in Class 4, Mridul and two other boys used to hide my bag and call me "Chipku" because I stood too close to the teacher. I thought it was my fault. Maybe I was annoying. Maybe I deserved it.

Every morning my stomach twisted into a knot. I told Amma I had a stomach ache. She gave me ajwain water. I drank it and didn't tell her the real reason.

I was scared that if I told, she'd march into school, and the boys would say I was a tattletale, and it would be worse.

It went on for two months. Then one day Amma found me crying in the bathroom and just held me until I talked. She met my teacher the next morning, quietly.

I wish I'd told her sooner. The secret was what kept it going.

— Chaitanya

qa.q: What did Amma give Chaitanya for the stomach ache?
qa.a: Ajwain water.

qa.q: Why did Chaitanya keep the real reason secret?
qa.a: Chaitanya felt afraid telling would make it worse and ashamed, thinking the bullying might be deserved.

qa.q: What does Chaitanya's story suggest to other children in the same place?
qa.a: That telling a trusted adult helps; keeping the secret out of fear and shame lets bullying continue.

qa.q: How might Amma have felt finding Chaitanya crying in the bathroom?
qa.a: She was probably shocked and worried, and she responded by holding Chaitanya until the words came.

grounding: Chaitanya recalls stomach aches, self-blame and hiding bullying from Amma out of fear, and how the secrecy let it continue until she found out.

passage: Class teacher's note, 3B, Wednesday. Baljeet has gone to the sick room with a stomach ache four mornings out of five this week, always before first period, never after lunch. Today I kept him back while the others went to PT and asked, "Is something at school making you feel bad?" He stared at his shoes and whispered, "Harish and his friends say I smell. It's my fault, I didn't bathe properly." He begged me not to tell his parents: "Papa will come and shout and it'll get worse." I told him it was not his fault, that he was right to tell me, and that I would help keep him safe. I informed the school counsellor, Mrs Anand, before the end of the day, and together we phoned his parents this evening to plan a calm meeting tomorrow.
